feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: What to know about the wacky first 5 weeks of the NFL season
entry.summary: It's been a topsy turvy NFL season so far. We check in with Jason Gay from The Wall Street Journal about what has surprised him after five weeks of football.

entry.title: Rise in accidents involving kids and e-bikes sparks debate about regulation
entry.summary: Emergency room departments are reporting soaring numbers of pediatric trauma accidents associated with micromobility devices. Experts and advocates agree that the federal government needs to step in.

entry.title: Remains of 11 Native children who died at a boarding school are returned to tribes
entry.summary: The Office of Army Cemeteries have returned the remains of 11 Native American and Alaska Native students who died while attending the Carlisle boarding school in Pennsylvania more than a century ago.

entry.title: A Korean city borrows an educational model from the U.S. amid AI concerns
entry.summary: Some South Korean schools have imported a U.S. educational model to boost literacy skills and independent thinking eroded by AI and a test-focused Korean educational system.

entry.title: Trump announced a partial Russia-Ukraine ceasefire. Did either country know about it?
entry.summary: Ukraine's leader says Russia is continuing to attack Ukraine and is ignoring an "energy ceasefire" declared by President Trump.

entry.title: Two Americans win Nobel for economics
entry.summary: This year's Nobel Prize for economics was awarded to two Americans, for their work on ways to limit booms and busts in the business cycle.

entry.title: Oil-heated households in Northeast strained by rising fuel prices
entry.summary: Rising fuel prices are stressing household budgets in the Northeast, where many rely on heating oil to warm their homes.

entry.title: Sauna research gathers steam
entry.summary: Leading researchers in heat exposure are coming together to reach a consensus on what we know — and don't — about the health benefits of sauna and its potential for treating and preventing disease.

entry.title: Many Iranians who go to Turkey to find jobs are exploited
entry.summary: Desperate Iranians are finding work in Turkey to make ends meet, but many are being exploited and left with nothing but more debt.

entry.title: Farmers say they'll take the relief of Trump's EO — but they're still hurting
entry.summary: President Trump says his Monday executive order temporarily suspending federal taxes on diesel will be a big relief for farmers. Some farmers call it a campaign ploy with marginal impact.
